problem:
The value $V=V(t)$ of a certain art object $t$ years after its production can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t}=kV
$$

where $k>0$ is the growth rate. If it was initially worth $$2\,000,$ and $V(10)=10\,000$, calculate the value  of the growth rate $k$ to the nearest percent.
worked_solution:
We model the value of the art object using the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t}=kV.
$$

The solution to this equation is

$$
V(t)={V}_{0}\,{e}^{kt},
$$

where ${V}_{0}$ is the initial value.

We're told that  it was initially worth $$2\,000,$ so we have ${V}_{0}=2\,000.$

Therefore, the value $V$ at time $t$ is

$$
V(t)=2\,000\,{e}^{kt}.
$$

Finally, to find the value of $k,$ we substitute $V(10)=10\,000$ into the equation above and solve for $k,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V(10) & =2\,000\,{e}^{k\cdot 10} \\ 10\,000 & =2\,000\,{e}^{10k} \\ {e}^{10k} & =\frac{10\,000}{2\,000} \\ {e}^{10k} & =5 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{10k}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) \\ 10k & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) \\ k & =\frac{1}{10}\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) \\ k & ≈0.16\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $k≈16%,$ rounded to the nearest percent.
